lesson.arabic-paragraph-design.title_en: Building a paragraph: عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ, أَيْ, هَكَذَا
lesson.arabic-paragraph-design.family_en: One purpose, sentences that add to it, and words that link them
steps: A paragraph serves one purpose: a sentence that states it, sentences that support it, and an ending that rounds it off.
Each sentence should add something: an example, a reason or a result. The same claim again in new words adds nothing.
Bring in an example with عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ, and check it supports this claim, not a new topic.
Explain a word with أَيْ, that is: الْمُوَاصَلَاتُ الْعَامَّةُ، أَيِ الْحَافِلَاتُ وَالْقِطَارَاتُ, public transport, that is, buses and trains.
Round it off with هَكَذَا, in this way, to show where the paragraph has led.

examples.ar: الدَّرَّاجَةُ أَسْرَعُ مِنَ الْحَافِلَةِ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ.
examples.en: A bike is faster than the bus in town.

examples.ar: عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ، أَصِلُ إِلَى عَمَلِي فِي عَشْرِ دَقَائِقَ.
examples.en: For example, I get to work in ten minutes.
In this way I save time and money.

why.q_en: What's the difference between عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ and أَيْ?
why.a_en: عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ brings in one case among others: for example. أَيْ restates or explains what you've just said: that is. A bike is one example of a way to get around; "public transport, أَيْ buses and trains" names all of it.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase brings in an example?
selftest.why_en: خَاتِمَة names a part of a paragraph, and أَيْ explains: "that is".

selftest.q_en: Which sentence adds something to "Cycling saves time"?
choices: It takes me ten minutes instead of thirty.
Cycling is a way to save time.
Time can be saved by cycling.
selftest.answer: It takes me ten minutes instead of thirty.
selftest.why_en: The other two say the same claim again in new words.

lesson.arabic-formal-email.title_en: A formal email: أَرْجُو, مُرْفَق, شُكْرًا مُسْبَقًا
lesson.arabic-formal-email.family_en: Opening, the request, attachments and closing, politely and clearly

table.en: I have a question about the course

steps: A formal email says who it's for, why you're writing, what they need to know, and exactly what you're asking.
Open with the person's title and الْمُحْتَرَمُ, then a greeting: تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً.
Make the request plain. أَرْجُو, I'd be grateful for, is followed by what you ask for, usually as a verbal noun: أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ الْفَاتُورَةِ, please send the invoice.
To an office, or someone you don't know, use the plural "you": تَجِدُونَ, you will find.
Check names, dates and attachments before sending, and close with شُكْرًا مُسْبَقًا, thank you in advance.

examples.ar: أَكْتُبُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِخُصُوصِ التَّسْجِيلِ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ.
examples.en: I'm writing to you about registering for the course.

examples.ar: أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ الْبَرْنَامَجِ قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْخَمِيسِ.
examples.en: Please send the programme before Thursday.
Please find the certificate attached to this email.

why.q_en: Why أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ, with a noun, and not أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا?
why.a_en: Both are right. أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا uses أَنْ and a verb; أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ uses the verbal noun, which sounds more formal and suits an email to an office.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "thank you in advance"?
selftest.why_en: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا is "thank you very much", and عَفْوًا "you're welcome".
مُرْفَق describes a file or a photo sent with the email; the plural is مُرْفَقَات, attachments.

selftest.q_en: Writing to an office, how do you say "you will find"?
selftest.why_en: The plural "you" is the polite one in a formal email. تَجِدُ is to one man, and تَجِدِينَ to one woman.

lesson.arabic-summary-notes.title_en: Summarising: who said what, in fewer words
lesson.arabic-summary-notes.family_en: Reporting a source's points faithfully, and keeping your view apart
steps: A summary keeps the main points, and their limits, in fewer words.
Say whose point it is: يَرَى الْكَاتِبُ أَنَّ, the writer thinks that; أَشَارَ إِلَى, pointed to; أَضَافَ أَنَّ, added that.
قَدْ before a present verb means "may": قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ, it may help. Keep it, or you make the source sound surer than it is.
Notes can be fragments; the summary needs full sentences with clear links between them.
Keep your own view out of the source's points. If you add it, put it in its own sentence, starting فِي رَأْيِي.

examples.ar: أَشَارَ الْكَاتِبُ إِلَى أَنَّ الْمَشْرُوعَ قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ بَعْضَ الطُّلَّابِ.
examples.en: The writer pointed out that the project may help some students.

examples.ar: أَضَافَ أَنَّ النَّتَائِجَ مَا زَالَتْ أَوَّلِيَّةً.
examples.en: He added that the results are still preliminary.

examples.ar: بِشَكْلٍ عَامٍّ، تَدْعُو الْمَقَالَةُ إِلَى الصَّبْرِ.
examples.en: Overall, the article calls for patience.

why.q_en: Why أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ, with both إِلَى and أَنَّ?
why.a_en: أَشَارَ takes إِلَى before what it points to. When that's a whole statement, أَنَّ brings it in: أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ الْمَشْرُوعَ مُفِيدٌ, he pointed out that the project is useful.

selftest.q_en: The source says قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ. Which summary keeps its meaning?
selftest.why_en: قَدْ with a present verb is "may": keep the limit.

selftest.q_en: Where does your own opinion go?
choices: in a separate sentence, marked as yours
selftest.answer: in a separate sentence, marked as yours
selftest.why_en: Keep the source's account and your view apart.

lesson.arabic-orthography-editing.title_en: Checking your spelling: ة, ى and where a hamza sits
lesson.arabic-orthography-editing.family_en: The letters learners mix up, the hamza's seat, and Arabic punctuation

table.en: the "tied t" at the end of a word
the "shortened alif": written short, said as a long ā at the end of a word

steps: Edit in passes: first the meaning and the order, then one spelling pattern at a time.
ة, the تَاءٌ مَرْبُوطَةٌ, ends a feminine noun and is said -a, or -at- before an ending: مَدِينَة, مَدِينَتُنَا. A plain ه is a real h: وَجْه, a face.
ى at the end, the أَلِفٌ مَقْصُورَةٌ, is a long ā: عَلَى, مُسْتَشْفَى. ي, with its dots, is ī or y: فِي.
At the end of a word, a hamza sits on the letter that matches the vowel before it: بَدَأَ after a, شَاطِئ after i, تَبَاطُؤ after u. After a sukūn or a long vowel it stands alone: جُزْء, سَمَاء.
Arabic's comma and question mark face the other way. Use them to help the reader, not to patch an unclear sentence.

words.en: started (hamza on an alif: a before it)

examples.en: We sat on the beach until the evening.

words.en: the beach (hamza on a ي-shape: i before it)

examples.en: Have you read the first part?

words.en: the part (hamza alone: a sukūn before it)

why.q_en: Why شَاطِئ, with the hamza on a ي-shape, but بَدَأَ with it on an alif?
why.a_en: The seat follows the vowel before the hamza: i before it in شَاطِئ, so a ي-shaped seat; a before it in بَدَأَ, so an alif.

selftest.q_en: Which letter writes the feminine ending of مَدِينَة?
selftest.why_en: ة is the تَاءٌ مَرْبُوطَةٌ. A plain ه is a real h.

selftest.q_en: Where does the hamza sit in بَدَأَ?
selftest.why_en: The vowel before it is a.
A question mark is عَلَامَةُ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ.

lesson.arabic-feedback-rewrite.family_en: The words for drafts and corrections, and how to make feedback stick
steps: Feedback helps when you understand a correction well enough to use it in a new sentence.
Sort the comments: meaning, order, grammar, spelling. Fix the meaning first.
Pick two or three patterns that keep coming back, rather than changing every sentence at once.
Grammar comments often name a word's gender: مُذَكَّر, masculine, or مُؤَنَّث, feminine. Words that describe it, or point to it, must match.
Keep your first مُسَوَّدَة, so you can see what changed and why.

examples.en: The teacher corrected the mistakes in my draft.

examples.ar: أَعَدْتُ كِتَابَةَ الْفِقْرَةِ بَعْدَ قِرَاءَةِ التَّعْلِيقَاتِ.
examples.en: I rewrote the paragraph after reading the comments.

examples.ar: تَحَسَّنَتْ كِتَابَتِي كَثِيرًا فِي الشَّهْرِ الْأَخِيرِ.
examples.en: My writing has improved a lot in the last month.

why.q_en: Why أَعَدْتُ, with a short a, from أَعَادَ?
why.a_en: أَعَادَ has a long ā in the middle, and, as in قَالَ, قُلْتُ, it shortens before an ending that starts with a consonant. Here the short vowel stays a: أَعَدْتُ, I did again.

selftest.q_en: You get twenty comments. What do you do first?
choices: fix the meaning, then two or three repeated patterns
selftest.answer: fix the meaning, then two or three repeated patterns
selftest.why_en: A few patterns you understand do more than many changes you don't.
